name: Svoi Kozyri
description: Svoi Kozyri (Russian: 'My Own Trumps' or 'Your Trumps') is a Russian card game where players have their own personal trump suit. It is a shedding game for 2-4 players. The objective is to get rid of all your cards. The twist is that if you lead a card of your own trump suit, it is powerful for you, but attacking others with their trumps forces them to defend heavily.

content.text: Svoi Kozyri (Russian: 'My Own Trumps' or 'Your Trumps') is a Russian card game where players have their own personal trump suit. It is a shedding game for 2-4 players. The objective is to get rid of all your cards. The twist is that if you lead a card of your own trump suit, it is powerful for you, but attacking others with their trumps forces them to defend heavily.

Svoi Kozyri (Russian: "one's own trumps") is a single-attack beating game; the earliest printed descriptions date from the 19th century. It survived as Vsyak svoi kozyri ("everyone has their own trumps") though rarely played today. Some sources consider it an elaboration of the Czech game Sedma. A two-player variant was brought to Cambridge by mathematician A.S. Besikovitch and published as "Challenge" in the Pan Book of Card Games; it was reportedly popular in Belarus in the countryside.
Two, three, or four players; best for four. Each player has a different trump suit agreed before play.
Standard Russian 36-card pack: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each of the four French suits.

Any player deals first; then the loser of each hand deals. Dealer shuffles, optional cut by player to dealer's right, then deals all 36 cards clockwise one at a time. Before play, players with sixes give them to the player who has that suit as trumps so each player has at least one trump.

items.text: Regional pick-up counts: The number of cards picked up when not beating varies in different parts of Russia (e.g. 3, 5, or whole pile).
Besikovich's game: Two-player variant with all cards exposed and symmetric deal; alternative to beating is to take the whole play pile. Published as Challenge in Pan Book of Card Games.
